name: transparent overlay autotile for the edges of a cracked concrete slab pavement on dirt: only the broken edge is drawn — rounded dirt bites eaten into the concrete from the open sides, a dark 1px broken lip under south breaks, lit broken rims, and loose concrete chunks lying on the dirt; the slab field underneath shows through so its seams and cracks run right up to the break
label: wasteland_ruins/slab-break

surfaces.part: large cracked concrete slab block (upper right) with seams and cracks
concrete strips and L-shaped edge pieces (left and centre)
loose concrete chunks on the dirt

answer.evidence: This is a flat overlay seen straight down. Concrete pieces lie on a dirt field, and the slab seams and cracks are drawn as top-down lines. Only a 1px dark lip under south breaks hints at depth. No part has a vertical front face of 3 or more rows, no eave shadow, and no ellipse. The column scans show only alternating dirt and concrete runs with no front-edge line. The result is a flat decal with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass reference, with 0% near-flat coverage. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the lips and seams are tinted rather than sticker-black. The concrete ramp is shallow, though: roughly light speckle, mid grey, dark grey and a seam tone, about 4 steps against Beodeul's 5-6. There are only 12 distinct colours overall (the grass reference has 80). The slab fragments show little per-chunk highlighting or shading. The loose chunks and rims are mostly one mid grey with a few speckle dots, so they read thinner and flatter than the paving reference's stone-by-stone shading. The dirt has some grain but only 3-4 browns. Since the call is close and this is a shallow ramp, I fail it rather than give it the benefit of the doubt.

The silhouette is a full-width tile sheet (256 px wide in every row). There is no ellipse, roof, or eave, so the piece is a flat top-down decal, which matches the 'flat' kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ground-kind overlay and the references (grass, paving) are the same kind. Measured facts: 5 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving and 3 for the grass; 0% near-flat coverage; 0% neutral dark edge pixels. The dark lips and rims lean brown/blue-grey rather than black, so the outline reads as a dark material tone, and I see no sticker-style black line. The weak points are ramp depth and craft. Concrete chunks show about 4 steps (light rim, mid, speckle, dark lip) against the paving's 6-7 with per-stone shading. The dirt is a fine, evenly scattered noise of about 3 browns with no clumps or grain structure. Only 12 distinct colours exist in the whole sheet against 80 for the grass, and the concrete interior is mostly one speckled grey with thin crack lines. It has no flat fills and passes on tinted outlines, but it is shallower than the Beodeul standard in shading steps and tile richness. Doubt resolves to fail.

The column scans show only alternating ground texture bands and flat grey patches, with no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical front face of 3 or more rows. The thin dark lines are slab seams and the 1px lip under the south breaks, not a south-facing vertical face. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours across dirt and concrete combined. The concrete ramp is about 4 steps (light rim, light grey, mid grey, dark seam or lip). The paving reference carries 6-7 tones per tile, with per-stone shading and tinted dark edges. Measured facts: the candidate shows 5 visible tones per tile against 7 for paving and 3 for grass. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted rather than black. The dirt has speckle and clump texture, and the concrete has fine speckle, so there are no flat fills. Weaknesses: the concrete bites and chunks read as thin, blobby cut-outs. The lit rims and south lips are only about 1px wide, with little stepped shading across the broken edges. The chunks look like flat grey stickers on the dirt rather than individually shaded stones. The overall tonal depth is a notch below the paving reference, so a careful artist would not accept it next to the reference without calling it flatter.
